text:
Maya: hey team :wave: quick question — what's the recommended place to post after-hours infra noise? if something noisy but not P0 happens at 7:30pm, do we ping #oncall, #eng, or DM the oncall person?

Devon: short answer: post in #oncall for anything that might need immediate attention. if it's just FYI and won't impact users, drop it in #eng with a clear subject like 'after-hours FYI'. :white_check_mark:

Maya: got it — and for exceptions (e.g., CI flakey during deploy) — should i still use #oncall or escalate to SRE@ pager?

Alex: escalate to @oncall (via #oncall) if it looks like it will degrade prod. otherwise #eng + screenshot is fine. if in doubt, ping oncall privately and then post the summary in the channel.

Leah: also pls include a short checklist in the post: what happened, trying steps, impact (prod/alpha/dev), and tags like `#deploy`, `#CI`. example: `Deploy failed: staging, retrying; impact: none; logs: <link>` — helps oncall triage faster.

Samir: FYI you can use the incident bot to create an incident ticket from slack: `/incident create` or click the :rotating_light: button in #oncall. saves typing.

Maya: perfect — is there a way to temporarily exempt a thread from quiet-hours notification rules? i don't want mobile pings for non-urgent updates.

Devon: yes — two options: 1) add `no-notify` in the body and use the onboard-bot tag like `@onboard-bot no-notify` for FYI-only, 2) alternatively, use DND or mute the channel on your phone. we try to avoid changing global quiet-hours for single posts.

it-admin: system note: automated deploy alerts go to #release-war-room and are rate-limited after 21:00 local. if teams need exceptions for a scheduled maintenance window, file a calendar event under the 'Ops Exceptions' calendar and mention #oncall so the bot applies a temporary rule.

Maya: thanks — how do i use the onboard-bot for this? i tried `@onboard-bot help` but got a wall of links. any quick snippet?

onboard-bot: hi Maya! quick commands:
• `@onboard-bot no-notify` — mark this thread as FYI (suppresses mobile pushes for role-based recipients)
• `/incident create` — start an incident (prompts for severity)
• `@onboard-bot runbook <name>` — respond with the runbook link
More docs: https://intranet.redwood/ops/quiet-hours (useful checklist + examples)

Alex: pro tip — when posting in #eng during quiet hours, start the message with `FYI (no-pager)` to make intent explicit. saves a few pings.

Leah: also, mention timeframe for follow-ups, e.g., 'will follow up tomorrow @10am' if you don't want people to try to fix it at midnight.

Maya: ok thanks — last q: where do new hires ask beginner setup questions (vpn, laptop imaging) without cluttering product channels?

Devon: #new-hires for onboarding questions and #help for IT issues. if it's a code/tool-specific question, drop into the relevant team channel and prefix with `newbie:`.

Samir: and DM the person listed as your buddy for hands-on walkthroughs. buddy list is in the welcome doc.

Maya: awesome — super clear. thanks everyone :raised_hands:

Leah: welcome again! ping any of us if you get stuck.

Devon: +1. and remember to subscribe to the ops status alerts: `/subscribe ops-status` — you'll get minimal but important updates.

Maya: subscribed. night folks :)

(onboard-bot automated message): pinned doc: https://intranet.redwood/onboarding/channel-rules — quick read, 3 min.
